title: Evidence-Grounded ASR Semantic Consequence Rubric
principles: Answer G1, G2, S1-S4, C1, and C2 independently. A semantic difference does not by itself determine recoverability or reader impact, and a visible surface difference does not by itself establish a semantic difference. Reason from complete sentences, but for evidence copy the shortest useful exact span; leave optional evidence empty rather than reconstructing or normalizing a long quote.

Interpret the aligned edit by comparing the actual complete reference_text and hypothesis_text; use the spans to locate it, not to hide sentence-level word order or clause-force changes. Keep alignment boundary quality separate from content. Repetition and neighboring spill are form effects when the resulting sentence preserves the same claim. An unexpected non-language symbol embedded where a lexical connector is required is not ordinary punctuation and leaves that relation unresolved.

A deletion within the same aligned lexical unit is a semantic or item difference when it leaves an informative word, predicate, name, technical term, identifier, or value incomplete and the hypothesis contains no complete recognized item. Contextual guessability is not full recovery. A proper-name spelling is a form variant only when it is an established rendering that still uniquely identifies the same entity, not merely because it is phonetically close.

Discourse markers, fillers, code-switched grammatical equivalents, conventional spoken forms, ordinary homophones in a uniquely constraining collocation, and grammatical ellipsis are form-only when the complete sentence still gives the same core claim and uniquely preserves the same participant. A change in a pronoun's person, number, possessor, or specific referent is a relation difference; C2 separately determines whether that relation is central or incidental.

For C2, MATERIAL and CRITICAL require a changed or unresolved core fact, event, identifiable entity or term, value, specific participant, logical condition, clause force, stance, or conclusion. A changed specific possessor is MATERIAL when it changes whose action, property, accomplishment, ownership, or responsibility is asserted. Repeated speech, non-possessive determiners, demonstratives, awkward wording, or an incidental local difference in discourse, degree, quantification, or generic inclusive reference is NONE or MINOR when the same central claim remains clear.

questions.question: Are the spans a plausible local alignment of the same ASR edit location, regardless of whether their meanings differ?

definitions.VALID: The spans occupy the same local edit position and their boundaries support comparison. A substitution may be VALID even when the two spans have very different meanings.
definitions.PARTIALLY_VALID: The spans broadly correspond, but one boundary includes or omits nearby material.
definitions.INVALID: The spans were paired from unrelated positions or the boundaries are so wrong that the highlighted local error is not the actual ASR edit. Do not choose INVALID merely because the meanings differ.
definitions.UNSCORABLE: There is insufficient information to judge alignment validity.

questions.question: Are the reference, hypothesis, and available context sufficient to judge the semantic consequence?

definitions.SCORABLE: The visible evidence supports a reliable consequence judgment.
definitions.UNSCORABLE: The reference is defective, required context is absent, or multiple materially different interpretations remain plausible.

questions.question: Does the error add, remove, change, or leave unexpressed a fact, event, action, state, predicate, lexical connector, or proposition?

definitions.NO_CHANGE: The proposition or event is preserved.
definitions.MINOR_FORM_CHANGE: Wording, fluency, discourse form, repetition, determiner choice, or grammar changes without changing the proposition. This includes a discourse marker, code-switched grammatical equivalent, repeated fragment, demonstrative, or recoverable grammatical omission when the complete sentence still expresses the same event and central informative content.
definitions.SEMANTIC_CHANGE: A fact, event, action, state, predicate, informative object, lexical connector, or other propositional content is added, removed, replaced, or left incomplete. A deletion inside the same aligned content word counts when the full hypothesis contains no complete recognized item. An unexpected non-language symbol occupying a word or connector position leaves that content unexpressed; do not silently read the missing word through it. Do not infer truncation when adjacent or repeated material completes the expression, and do not mark SEMANTIC_CHANGE for awkward grammar or boundary spill when the complete sentence still expresses the same proposition.
definitions.UNCERTAIN: The evidence does not support a reliable choice.

questions.question: Does the aligned expression itself represent and change an entity, attribute, professional term, number, time, date, unit, version, or quantity?

definitions.NO_CHANGE: The aligned expression represents an entity, attribute, term, or value and preserves the same item.
definitions.MINOR_FORM_CHANGE: A recognized spelling, transliteration, abbreviation, spoken form, or established rendering differs while the hypothesis still uniquely identifies the same entity, professional term, attribute, or value. Phonetic closeness, small edit distance, or contextual guessability alone does not establish a recognized variant, especially for proper names and identifiers.
definitions.SEMANTIC_CHANGE: The identity, attribute, professional term, parameter, or value differs, is truncated into an incomplete item, or is no longer uniquely identifiable from the hypothesis. An altered proper name, technical term, identifier, or value is semantic unless the hypothesis itself supplies a recognized complete variant that uniquely preserves the same item.
definitions.UNCERTAIN: The evidence does not support a reliable choice.
definitions.N_A: The aligned expression does not itself represent an entity, attribute, professional term, number, time, date, unit, version, or quantity. Ordinary predicates, discourse markers, and neighboring clause-linking material belong here rather than being invented as entities.

questions.question: Does the error change clause type, question versus assertion force, negation, modality, certainty, condition, comparison, quantifier scope, tense, or completion status?

definitions.NO_CHANGE: Clause type, logical force, scope, and completion status are preserved.
definitions.MINOR_FORM_CHANGE: A surface, auxiliary, or grammatical form changes without changing clause type, logical force, scope, or completion status.
definitions.SEMANTIC_CHANGE: Question versus assertion force, negation, modality, certainty, condition, comparison, quantifier scope, tense, or completion status changes in the actual complete reference_text and hypothesis_text. In unpunctuated transcripts, determine clause force from syntax: auxiliary-before-subject interrogative order versus subject-before-auxiliary declarative order is a question-versus-assertion change. Do not reconstruct one sentence from the highlighted spans when the visible complete sentences have different word order or clause force. A contraction, auxiliary variant, or incidental degree nuance is not enough when the central claim retains the same force.
definitions.UNCERTAIN: The evidence does not support a reliable choice.

questions.question: Does the error change participant roles, subject/object, reference, causality, temporal relation, viewpoint attribution, or another semantic relation?

definitions.NO_CHANGE: Roles and semantic relations are preserved.
definitions.MINOR_FORM_CHANGE: The wording changes without changing an informative participant or relation. A recoverable subject ellipsis, agreement form, filler, or boundary artifact belongs here only when the complete sentence uniquely preserves the same participant, person, number, possession, and role.
definitions.SEMANTIC_CHANGE: A participant, role, referent, cause, temporal relation, viewpoint attribution, grammatical person, number, or possessor changes or becomes unresolved. Record a pronoun substitution as a relation change when it denotes a distinct participant or participant set; whether that difference is consequential belongs to C2, not S4.
definitions.UNCERTAIN: The evidence does not support a reliable choice.

questions.question: Using only the ASR hypothesis and available reader context, can a reasonable reader uniquely and reliably recover the original meaning?

definitions.FULLY_RECOVERABLE: The hypothesis and reader-visible context support one informative interpretation matching the intended meaning. This may include a discourse or grammatical variation, code-switched equivalent, conventional spoken form, ordinary homophone in a uniquely constraining conventional expression, or ellipsis whose participant remains uniquely fixed. An unexpected non-language symbol inside a lexical phrase is not silently normalized when the missing connector or relation is unresolved. A changed pronoun does not qualify when person, number, possessor, or specific referent remains different or unresolved. A proper name, technical term, identifier, or value must remain uniquely identified by a complete recognized form in the hypothesis.
definitions.PARTIALLY_RECOVERABLE: The broad event or topic is clear, but an informative predicate, entity, term, value, participant, logical condition, stance, or clause force remains unresolved. Context may suggest the missing detail without uniquely preserving it.
definitions.NOT_RECOVERABLE: The visible hypothesis supports a different informative interpretation or multiple materially different interpretations. An incomplete content word, different valid informative word, unrecognized proper-name spelling, corrupted technical term, identifier, or parameter counts as unrecovered when the hypothesis itself does not uniquely preserve the intended item.
definitions.UNSCORABLE: The context or intended meaning is too incomplete to assess recoverability.

boundary_examples: A sentence-final or boundary-local deletion that leaves an informative word visibly incomplete is not fully recoverable merely because its likely completion can be guessed.
A recognized transliteration or established spelling variant may be fully recoverable; a merely plausible phonetic spelling of a proper name is not enough.
An ordinary-word homophone can be fully recoverable when the complete hypothesis and a conventional collocation permit only the intended informative reading.

An omitted grammatical subject can be fully recoverable when the surrounding clause uniquely preserves who participates and what happened; a changed pronoun with a different person, number, or possessor is not repaired merely by knowing the topic.
An unexpected symbol embedded inside an otherwise lexical phrase is not treated as harmless punctuation when a required connector or relation is no longer expressed.
Recovering only the topic while an informative term, identity, value, relation, clause force, or predicate remains uncertain is PARTIALLY_RECOVERABLE.

questions.question: How much would a reasonable reader's interpretation of the ASR hypothesis differ from the speaker's intended meaning?

definitions.NONE: The reader obtains the same informative interpretation; any difference is formal or fully recoverable from reader-visible evidence.
definitions.MINOR: The aligned edit creates a noticeable local difference, but the complete sentences retain the same central predicate, core arguments, logical force, stance, and conclusion. This includes boundary continuation, repeated or redundant speech, speech-event markup, a fluency repair inside repetition or malformed speech, discourse wording, a non-possessive determiner or demonstrative, conventional spoken or written form, awkward grammar, generic reference, recoverable subject omission, or an incidental degree or quantifier nuance. A genuine local S1-S4 difference can still be MINOR when these sentence-level invariants remain intact. A changed specific possessor is not merely a determiner variation.
definitions.MATERIAL: The aligned edit changes or leaves unresolved a core fact, predicate, entity identity, key term, informative object or parameter, value, specific participant or responsibility, logical condition, question-versus-assertion force, stance, or conclusion. Shared topic alone is insufficient if one of these differs. A specific possessor change is MATERIAL when it changes whose action, property, accomplishment, ownership, or responsibility is asserted. This also includes an incomplete informative word, unrecognized proper name or technical term, or unresolved connector replaced by a non-language symbol when that information is needed for the central interpretation. A SEMANTIC_CHANGE answer alone is insufficient when the complete sentences preserve the same predicate, core arguments, force, stance, and conclusion.
definitions.CRITICAL: The error reverses a central conclusion, negation, key entity, responsibility, safety fact, or other high-risk meaning.
definitions.UNSCORABLE: The available evidence cannot support a reliable impact judgment.

boundary_examples: A discourse marker, filler, inflection, code-switched grammatical equivalent, conventional spoken form, generic pronoun, recoverable ellipsis, boundary continuation, repeated wording, redundant detail, or speech-event markup is NONE or MINOR when the same central claim remains clear.
An unresolved incomplete predicate or content word, entity identity, key term, value, or question-versus-assertion force is MATERIAL when it carries the sentence's central information.
A real difference in degree, quantification, reference, or grammar is MINOR when it is incidental and leaves the same central predicate, core arguments, logical force, stance, and conclusion clear.
Judge impact independently after S1-S4 and C1; neither SEMANTIC_CHANGE nor NOT_RECOVERABLE automatically implies MATERIAL.

When one version contains repeated or malformed speech, compare the complete propositions: a local lexical replacement is MINOR if it functions as a fluency repair and preserves the same predicate, participants, topic, and stance.
